newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Analysts divided over Portugal rate cut prospects.
newsitem.headline: Analysts divided over Portugal rate cut prospects.

text.p: Analysts were divided over whether Portugal would cut its key repo rate tomorrow even if Spain does so, because of uncertainty over the inflation outlook.

"There is a reasonable possibility that the Bank of Portugal could cut rates, but I think it should wait until there is greater certainty over the inflation trend," said Valetim Martins of Lisbon broker Siemca.

Isabel Cabral of broker Fincor said: "Consumer price inflation should be showing a more favourable trend now, the escudo is strong and the 1997 budget is practically approved. If Spain lowers rates, the Bank of Portugal will do so too."
She said that if the Bank of Spain cuts its repo rate by 25 basis points, the Bank of Portugal would do the same and both rates would stand at 7.00 percent.
The Bank of Portugal is due to review its key rates tomorrow on the eve of a new 10-day commercial bank reserve period.
"Just because there is a strong conviction that the Bank of Spain will cut rates does not mean that the Bank of Portugal will do so too," said Carla Rebelo of Banco Finantia.

"The empirical evidence of the last two years shows that the Bank of Portugal is not tied to the Bank of Spain in its rate decisions. The Bank of Spain has been more volatile than the Bank of Portugal."
Martins said: "I believe inflation is coming down, but the Bank of Portugal has to be more sure of this in order to take a decision to cut rates."
Rebelo said the increases in inflation in recent months were explained by special factors and that the underlying trend in prices was steady or falling.
Portugal's repo rate has stood at 7.25 percent since August 26 and the absorption rate at which it drains funds from the money market has remained at 6.80 percent since April 19.
Even though he did not expect a rate cut tomorrow, Martins said the repo and absorption rate should drop to 7.00 and 6.50 percent respectively by the end of the year, an identical forecast to Cabral.
"The Bank of Portugal must have reasons not to move its rates much," said one operator who asked not to be identified.

"When the Bundesbank cut its repo rate by 30 basis points in August, the Bank of Portugal followed suit less than proportionately (cutting by 25 bp) and it appeared to have cut the rates because other countries did so."
Another dealer, who asked not to be identified, said there was a clear expectation Portuguese official rates would fall as cash and futures rates eased towards the absorption rate level.
Three month money rates stood at 7.00/7.05 percent and six- and 12-month money rates were between 6.90 and 6.96 percent.
The escudo hit a two-year high against the mark today, standing at 101.25/30 per mark at 1554 GMT.
